The `testToClass_object` test in `org.apache.commons.lang3.ClassUtilsTest` is calling the `toClass` method from `org.apache.commons.lang3.ClassUtils` with an array that contains a mixture of objects including `null`. The `toClass` method is supposed to return an array of `Class` objects corresponding to the classes of the input objects.

Looking at the implementation of the `toClass` method in `org.apache.commons.lang3.ClassUtils`, it handles cases where the input array is `null` or empty, but it does not handle the case where the input array contains `null` elements. When the input array contains a `null` element, the `getClass()` method will throw a `NullPointerException` when called on the `null` object.

This lack of handling for `null` elements in the input array is likely causing the `NullPointerException` mentioned in the current bug report when the `toClass` method is called with an array containing `null`.

To fix this issue, the `toClass` method should be modified to check for `null` elements in the input array before calling `getClass()` on them. This can be done by adding a null check before accessing the class of each element in the array.

Next, I will suggest the method that needs to be fixed to address this issue.
The issue can be addressed by fixing the `org.apache.commons.lang3.ClassUtils.toClass(java.lang.Object[])` method. 

The method that needs to be fixed is:
`org.apache.commons.lang3.ClassUtils.toClass(java.lang.Object[])`

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
